target.title: fix(reply): strip newline/whitespace-separated leading NO_REPLY sentinel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103735. Follow-up to #30916 and #30955.

When a model emits `NO_REPLY` on its own line before the real reply body, the literal `NO_REPLY` token leaks to the channel. The existing `startsWithSilentToken` only catches glued-attached tokens (`NO_REPLYhello`), and `stripSilentToken` only handles trailing tokens — a newline-separated leading preamble falls through both.

## Root Cause

`startsWithSilentToken` uses a glued-attached regex requiring `(?=[\p{L}\p{N}])`. A newline-separated leading token (`NO_REPLY\n\nWait...`) is not detected. The parallel announcement path in `subagent-announce.ts` has the same gap.

## Fix

Add `startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken` to the shared `tokens.ts` module. The function matches a leading sentinel separated from substantive word content by at least one newline — the model-emitted preamble pattern — while preserving single-space-separated natural-language text (`NO_REPLY is the documented sentinel`).

Apply the shared detection to **both** callers:
- `normalize-reply.ts` — normal reply delivery
- `subagent-announce.ts` — subagent announcement delivery (parallel path identified by ClawSweeper)

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/tokens.ts` | New `startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken` export + shared regex |
| `src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts` | 3 new tests for the shared function |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.ts` | Replace inline `\s+` logic with shared function call |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` | Updated test expectations (space-separated is now preserved) |
| `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts` | Added newline-separated detection (parallel announcement path) |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — OpenClaw main + PR patch, live Node.js import

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "import { startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken } from '...'"

✅ Newline preamble:    "NO_REPLY\n\nWait"         → true  (detected)
✅ Single newline:      "NO_REPLY\nWait"           → true  (detected)
✅ Padded + newline:    "  NO_REPLY  \n\nAnswer"   → true  (detected)
✅ Space-separated:     "NO_REPLY is the sentinel" → false (preserved)
✅ Double dash:         "NO_REPLY -- nope"         → false (preserved)
✅ Punctuation:         "NO_REPLY: explanation"     → false (preserved)
✅ Glued (existing):    "NO_REPLYhello"            → false (handled by startsWithSilentToken)
✅ Trailing (existing): "Hello NO_REPLY"           → false (handled by stripSilentToken)
```

### Mantis Telegram Desktop Proof

Mantis captured Telegram before/after GIFs: leading `NO_REPLY` preamble removed, substantive reply preserved.

### Vitest

```
✓ tokens.test.ts: startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken — 3 new tests
✓ reply-utils.test.ts: strips newline-separated leading NO_REPLY (#103735)
✓ reply-utils.test.ts: preserves space-separated leading NO_REPLY as substantive
✓ reply-utils.test.ts: suppresses when stripping leaves only whitespace
✓ reply-utils.test.ts: all existing NO_REPLY tests pass unchanged
```
